_comment: Greenhaven shared PostgreSQL egg, Pelican PLCN_v1. One of these per panel; every Greenhaven world server points its RPG_DB at it. Pair: server-architecture/greenhaven-egg.json.
name: Greenhaven PostgreSQL
author: otterdays
description: Shared PostgreSQL for the Greenhaven world servers. ONE TCP port (allocate it on the node's PRIVATE IP, never the public one). pg_hba only accepts password logins from 10/8, 172.16/12 and 192.168/16, so a public allocation is refused anyway. Data lives in data/ and survives reinstall. A pg_dump runs every BACKUP_HOURS into backups/ - the panel's volume backup is not a consistent database copy. Start this server BEFORE any world server; worlds crash on boot without it. Connection string for each world: postgres://<user>:<password>@<node-internal-ip>:<port>/<db>.

config.startup: {"done": "database system is ready to accept connections"}

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Greenhaven shared PostgreSQL install. Runs as root in the official postgres image.
# Safe to re-run: an existing cluster in data/ is kept untouched (your saves survive reinstall).
set -e
cd /mnt/server
mkdir -p data backups
: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?POSTGRES_PASSWORD must be set (long random string)}"
: "${POSTGRES_USER:=game_user}"
: "${POSTGRES_DB:=game_db}"
chown postgres:postgres data backups
if [ -s data/PG_VERSION ]; then
  echo "Existing cluster found in data/ (PG $(cat data/PG_VERSION)). Keeping it; saves survive reinstall."
else
  pw="$(mktemp)"; printf '%s' "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}" > "$pw"; chown postgres "$pw"
  echo "initdb (${POSTGRES_USER} is the superuser of this cluster) ..."
  su postgres -c "initdb -D /mnt/server/data -U '${POSTGRES_USER}' --pwfile='$pw' --auth=scram-sha-256 -E UTF8 --locale=C.UTF-8"
  rm -f "$pw"
fi
# Install-phase auth: the socket-only server below is reachable by nobody but this script, so the
# socket is trusted here. Password-only rules replace this before the server is ever exposed. Without
# this, createdb would wait for a password on a TTY the installer does not have and hang forever.
echo 'local   all   all   trust' > data/pg_hba.conf
chown postgres data/pg_hba.conf
su postgres -c "pg_ctl -D /mnt/server/data -o \"-c listen_addresses='' -k /tmp\" -w start"
if su postgres -c "psql -w -h /tmp -U '${POSTGRES_USER}' -d postgres -Atc \"SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='${POSTGRES_DB}'\"" | grep -q 1; then
  echo "Database ${POSTGRES_DB} already exists."
else
  echo "Creating database ${POSTGRES_DB} ..."
  su postgres -c "createdb -w -h /tmp -U '${POSTGRES_USER}' '${POSTGRES_DB}'"
fi
su postgres -c "pg_ctl -D /mnt/server/data -w stop"
# Only the node's private networks may connect, and only with a password. Docker NAT makes every
# world-server container show up from a 172.x/10.x/192.168.x source, never from the public internet.
cat > data/pg_hba.conf <<'HBA'
local   all   all                    scram-sha-256
host    all   all   127.0.0.1/32     scram-sha-256
host    all   all   ::1/128          scram-sha-256
host    all   all   10.0.0.0/8       scram-sha-256
host    all   all   172.16.0.0/12    scram-sha-256
host    all   all   192.168.0.0/16   scram-sha-256
HBA
chown postgres data/pg_hba.conf
# Runtime wrapper: postgres in the foreground, a pg_dump loop beside it. The panel's Backups tab
# only tars the volume, which is not a consistent Postgres copy; the dumps in backups/ are.
cat > start.sh <<'RUN'
#!/bin/bash
cd /home/container
PORT="${SERVER_PORT:-5432}"
backup_loop() {
  export PGPASSWORD="${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
  while true; do
    sleep "$(( ${BACKUP_HOURS:-6} * 3600 ))"
    f="backups/${POSTGRES_DB}_$(date +%F_%H%M).sql.gz"
    if pg_dump -h /tmp -p "$PORT" -U "$POSTGRES_USER" "$POSTGRES_DB" | gzip > "$f"; then
      echo "[backup] wrote $f"
      ls -1t backups/*.sql.gz 2>/dev/null | tail -n +"$(( ${BACKUP_KEEP:-28} + 1 ))" | xargs -r rm -f
    else
      echo "[backup] FAILED"; rm -f "$f"
    fi
  done
}
postgres -D /home/container/data -p "$PORT" -k /tmp \
  -c listen_addresses='*' -c max_connections="${MAX_CONNECTIONS:-100}" \
  -c shared_buffers="${SHARED_BUFFERS:-128MB}" -c log_min_messages=warning &
PG=$!
if [ "${BACKUP_HOURS:-6}" != "0" ]; then backup_loop & BK=$!; fi
trap 'kill -INT $PG 2>/dev/null; [ -n "$BK" ] && kill $BK 2>/dev/null' INT TERM
# The image's tini -g signals the whole group, so the first wait returns the moment the panel
# stops us; the second one keeps the container alive until postgres has finished its shutdown.
wait $PG
wait $PG
RUN
chmod +x start.sh
chown -R postgres:postgres /mnt/server
echo "Install complete. Point every Greenhaven world at postgres://${POSTGRES_USER}:<password>@<node-internal-ip>:<this server's port>/${POSTGRES_DB}"
exit 0

variables.name: Database name
variables.description: Database every Greenhaven world shares. Admin-only; changing it after install does nothing (the cluster is already created).

variables.name: Database user
variables.description: Superuser of this cluster and the user the worlds log in as. Admin-only; fixed at install.

variables.name: Database password
variables.description: Set BEFORE the first install; it is baked into the cluster. Use 32+ random characters. The same value goes into each world's RPG_DB URL. Admin-only, secret.

variables.name: Max connections
variables.description: Each world server holds a small pool plus one LISTEN connection. 100 covers ~10 worlds with room for psql.

variables.name: Shared buffers
variables.description: Postgres cache. About a quarter of the RAM you give this server (128MB for a 512MB container).

variables.name: Backup interval (hours)
variables.description: pg_dump into backups/ every N hours. 0 disables (do not, this database is the only copy of every save).

variables.name: Backups to keep
variables.description: Oldest dumps beyond this count are deleted. 28 x 6h = one week.
